provided_deck_matrix_assessment: The current proof set is still lean and structurally sound for this audit: 11 representative decks in `archetype-fixture-matrix.json` plus supplemental `CuteWarrior` in `supplemental-proof-decks.json`, with the universal matrix test running all 12 through no-block prepare validation.

The deck set covers many of the mechanic families that matter most for a pre-run config generator: ShadowPriest proves hero-power transform and aggro burn; CtAPaladin and BigShaman prove recruit; BigShaman adds deathrattle and cheat; PirateRogue and Kingslayer prove weapon pressure; Discolock proves discard; TreantDruid proves token or aura posture; ImbueMage proves hero-power plus Imbue and generated-entity adjacency; MechPala proves board scaling; Boarlock proves exact combo output; PirateDH proves hero-attack pirate pressure.
CuteWarrior is correctly kept supplemental. It expands low-curve Warrior acceptance coverage without turning a narrow acceptance proof into a twelfth representative output-competence row.

The matrix is broad enough to justify the repo's current no-block claim, but it does not directly deck-prove every mechanic listed in this audit. Dedicated Discover, Choose One, Secret, Freeze, Location, Tourist, Starship, Rewind, Herald, and Shatter coverage currently relies more on registry, drift, and micro-tests than on representative deck fixtures.

That split is acceptable for a slim HSConfig repo. For a pre-run no-block generator, the matrix should prove broad shell behavior and runtime safety, while mechanic-specific tests and drift reports carry the long tail of modern keyword coverage.
no_block_assessment: Nothing is blocked should continue to mean technical validity and load-safe apply first: the package is structurally valid, required files exist, runtime apply mode is `load_safe_apply`, and non-blocking mechanic visibility is present in operator reports.

Nothing is blocked should not mean every mechanic is first-class lowered. HSConfig's current direct, identity-gated direct, partial, and warning-only split is the correct way to separate runtime safety from semantic richness.

Identity-gated direct is the right boundary for `discover`, `choose_one`, and `hero_power_transform`: HSConfig may lower them directly only when exact option identity or transformed hero-power identity is resolved from source-backed evidence.

Partial coverage is the right boundary for `spellburst`, `miniaturize`, `quickdraw`, `honorable_kill`, `elusive`, `poisonous`, `imbue`, `freeze`, `location`, `secret`, `deathrattle`, `recruit`, and `generated_entity`: HSConfig lowers the safe posture or timing parts and leaves unresolved state, target, or random-pool behavior report-visible.

Warning-only coverage is the right boundary for `rewind`, `herald`, `shatter`, `kindred`, `tourist`, `starship`, `dredge`, and `tradeable`: they stay visible, non-silent, and non-blocking, but HSConfig must not invent new runtime rows for their signature actions.

Unknown-warning coverage is still the correct future fallback, but none of the requested mechanics are in that fallback bucket today. The repo now has explicit registered handling for every mechanic named in this audit.
skill_slimness_assessment: HSConfig remains appropriately slim because it uses a compact mechanic registry plus a non-blocking drift surface instead of widening the runtime package or importing HSTuner-style post-run concerns.

The live repo keeps modern mechanic coverage inside the pre-run boundary: reporting, semantic enrichment, suppression, and cautious lowering live in HSConfig; replay parsing, winrate tuning, candidate promotion, and post-game adaptation remain out of scope.

Keeping Rewind, Herald, Shatter, Kindred, Tourist, Starship, Dredge, and Tradeable as warning-only is a quality sign, not a weakness. It shows the repo is refusing to fabricate unsupported behavior just to claim wider coverage.

The deck matrix is also slim in the right way. The repo proves broad shell coverage with 11 representative rows and one supplemental row instead of adding one representative deck per new expansion keyword.

The only polish still worth doing is proof polish: a few more keyword-specific assertions would strengthen confidence without changing product scope, adding dependencies, or widening runtime write behavior.
hearthstone_semantic_coverage: Direct coverage is currently narrow and appropriate: `overload` lowers through `CARDID.json:BeforePlayCardBonus` plus `GlobalValues.json:deck_posture`, and `weapon` lowers through attack or play posture plus optional exact combo sequencing. These are real runtime surfaces, not report-only labels.

Identity-gated direct coverage is correctly explicit: `discover`, `choose_one`, and `hero_power_transform` are only fully lowerable when the exact choice identity or transformed hero-power identity is known. The operator bucket is `identity_gated_direct`, which is safer than pretending they are unconditional direct mechanics.

Partial coverage is broad and sensible for Wild deck preparation: `spellburst`, `miniaturize`, `quickdraw`, `honorable_kill`, `elusive`, `poisonous`, `imbue`, `freeze`, `location`, `secret`, `deathrattle`, `recruit`, and `generated_entity` all map to real posture or timing surfaces, but their one-shot state, hidden information, random pools, or exact target logic remain intentionally incomplete.

Warning-only coverage is now explicit, not accidental: `rewind`, `herald`, `shatter`, `kindred`, `tourist`, `starship`, `dredge`, and `tradeable` all resolve to registered report-only support. That is the correct no-block outcome for mechanics whose signature behavior depends on temporal replay, deck-construction identity, hidden choices, or novel card-state actions that do not have a documented normal-path VisionAI row.

Current card-data representation strengthens the case for the repo's split. On 2026-07-10, live collectible data showed Rewind, Herald, Shatter, Kindred, and Tourist as text-only mechanics, while Starship, Spellburst, Miniaturize, Quickdraw, Honorable Kill, Elusive, Poisonous, Discover, Tradeable, Overload, and Deathrattle appeared in explicit mechanics or tags. That means HSConfig needs both static semantics and drift detection, not just one layer.

Location and Weapon are already handled through card type, which matches the repo's current semantics well. Freeze, Secret, Recruit, Choose One, Dredge, and Imbue appear in mixed explicit and text-only forms, so the current combination of explicit support rows, text-pattern drift detection, and conservative warning boundaries is the right architecture.

Unknown-warning coverage is currently unused for the requested mechanic list, which is a meaningful improvement over earlier audit states. The repo now names all requested mechanics explicitly, even when the right result is still warning-only.
gaps_or_risks: Representative deck coverage is still weaker than registry coverage for several newer mechanics. Rewind, Herald, Shatter, Tourist, Kindred, and Starship are supported honestly, but mostly through support rows and drift tests rather than through dedicated deck-fixture proof.

Some modern mechanics rely heavily on text-only visibility in current public card data. Rewind, Herald, Shatter, Kindred, and Tourist are all text-only in the 2026-07-10 collectible probe, which means regressions in drift detection would hurt visibility faster than regressions in explicit mechanic-tag parsing.

Warning-only support is intentionally non-lowering. That keeps no-block behavior honest, but it also means decks built around Dredge, Tradeable, Tourist, Starship, Rewind, Herald, Shatter, or Kindred will remain descriptively covered rather than action-rich in the pre-run package.

Partial mechanics still hide long-tail state complexity. Generated random pools, exact secret timing, repeated location activations, Quickdraw drawn-this-turn state, Miniaturize copy sequencing, and Honorable Kill equality math are visible but not fully planned as first-class runtime actions.

Hearthstone mechanic drift is ongoing. Because this audit depends on `https://api.hearthstonejson.com/v1/latest/`, any new expansion or card-data schema change can move a mechanic from explicit to text-only or vice versa, so the audit should be refreshed whenever a new Wild-relevant set lands.
recommended_next_action: Add one compact modern-keyword regression fixture that asserts current text-only mechanics `rewind`, `herald`, `shatter`, `kindred`, and `tourist` remain visible in `mechanic_drift_report.json` and stay in their intended warning-only buckets without widening the representative deck matrix.
confidence: high: the verdict is consistent across the live support registry, operator docs, local tests that passed on 2026-07-10, official Blizzard mechanic announcements, and a same-day HearthstoneJSON collectible-card probe showing the current keyword mix.
